methods.label: Find the diameters, then use the right triangle
methods.explanation:
The semicircle measurements let us find two sides of the right triangle. Let \(r>0\) be the radius of the semicircle on \(AB\). Its area is half the area of a full circle, so
\[
\frac{\pi r^2}{2}=8\pi.
\]
Thus \(r^2=16\), and positivity gives \(r=4\). Since \(AB\) is its diameter, \(AB=8\).

Let \(R>0\) be the radius of the semicircle on \(AC\). Its curved arc is half a full circumference, with length \(\frac12(2\pi R)=\pi R\). Therefore \(\pi R=8.5\pi\), giving \(R=8.5\) and diameter \(AC=17\).

Because the triangle is right at \(B\), \(AC\) is the hypotenuse. The Pythagorean theorem gives
\[
BC^2=AC^2-AB^2
=17^2-8^2=225.
\]
A side length is positive, so \(BC=15\). The semicircle on \(BC\) has radius \(15/2=\boxed{7.5}\), choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
